newsitem.title: JAPAN: Debts at Japan bankrupt firms surge 181% in March.
newsitem.headline: Debts at Japan bankrupt firms surge 181% in March.

text.p: Debts held by Japanese companies that went bankrupt in March surged 180.9 percent from the same month last year to 1.42 trillion yen, private research firm Tokyo Shoko Research Ltd said on Monday.
The figure was up 91.3 percent from February, a Tokyo Shoko report said.
The number of bankruptcies in March increased 2.0 percent from a year earlier to 1,373, the report said. It was up 12.0 percent from February.
The surge in debt in March was largely due to a rise in debts held by finance and real estate companies which went under, the report said.

The number of large-scale bankruptcies, those with debts of more than one billion yen, hit 94 in March, the third-largest number ever for a single month, it said. Of the 94, 13 firms had debts of more than 10 billion yen.
The largest number of large-scale bankruptcies in a single month was 102 in December 1991, and the second-largest was 95 in February.

Tokyo Shoko also released a report on bankruptcies for the 1996/97 fiscal year, ended March 31. It said total debt at firms which went bankrupt in 1996/97 were up 7.2 percent from the previous year at 9.26 trillion yen.
It is the first time total debts of bankrupt firms have surpassed nine trillion yen in a fiscal year, the research firm said.
Nichiei Finance Co Ltd, which applied for liquidation in late 1996, became the first Japanese company on record to fail with debts of more than one trillion yen, Tokyo Shoko said.

The number of bankruptcy cases in 1996/97 fell 0.8 percent from the previous year to 15,030, the report said, but it was still the second successive year in which the number of bankruptcies had exceeded 15,000, it said.
